title: IA3 baseline versus Mirror activation views

strata: one-plane Givens rotation views on hidden activation
metrics: actual serialized shared model+task payload bytes

hypothesis: A one-angle Givens Mirror activation view can recover rotated task functions with lower task-state bytes than full IA3 channel scales, while IA3 should remain stronger for independent diagonal task variation.
physical_object: one frozen shared feature network and common downstream weights
mirror_coordinate: per-task Givens angle inserted at the hidden activation interface
logical_multiplicity: 8 task functions from one physical feature network
controls: native IA3 per-task diagonal activation scales
independent dense per-task activation transform upper control

development.allowed: validate forward shape, metric, fit and payload serialization; no fresh tuning

storage.authority: actual flat serialized inference payload bytes including shared weights, all task views and metadata

success_gate: Aligned Givens stratum: Mirror NRMSE <=0.01 and total payload <=80% of IA3 payload in each fresh world. Independent diagonal stratum maps where diagonal/private coordinates are necessary.
failure_gate: Mirror aligned NRMSE >0.05 or no storage reduction at matched quality; IA3 superiority on independent stratum is a scoped boundary, not an experiment-wide failure by itself.
boundaries: Synthetic frozen feature network only; no NLP or transformer quality claim.
Aligned rotation tasks are a feasibility regime; independent diagonal tasks test view mismatch.
Task IDs are given; routing is not studied.
